[[8:19|and my blossoms than choice silver|Et genimina mea argento electo]], that is, the outward works that proceed from me are better than the finest gold [so the print, *auro obrizo*, though the verse has "choice silver"].

paras.t: In viis justitiæ ambulo, id est, cum eis sum et procedo, qui juste vivunt, et gratiam ambulandi in viis justitiæ tribuo. Unde Moyses ait : In quo scire poterimus, invenisse nos gratiam in conspectu tuo, nisi ambulaveris nobiscum ? Apostolus quoque allegat quod in Levitico legitur, Ambulabo in eis : non quod incircumscriptibilis et invariabilis Deus mutet locum, sed ratione suorum effectuum hæc et consimilia de ipso dicuntur. Nam subditur : in medio semitarum judicii. Semitæ judicii, sunt præcepta et instituta, jura ac regulæ ex quibus proferuntur justa judicia, vel actus judiciorum in quibus Deo complacitum est : ideo in eis se esse, ambulareque perhibet modo prætacto.
paras.en: [[8:20|I walk in the way of justice|In viis justitiæ ambulo]], that is, I am with those who live justly and go forward with them, and I give the grace to walk in the ways of justice. Hence Moses says: [[Ex 33:16|how shall we be able to know|In quo scire poterimus]], [[Ex 33:16|that we have found grace in thy sight, unless thou walk with us|invenisse nos gratiam in conspectu tuo, nisi ambulaveris nobiscum]]? The Apostle too cites[[2 Cor 6:16||]] what we read in Leviticus: [[Lev 26:12|I will walk|Ambulabo]] in them: not that God, who cannot be circumscribed and does not change, changes place, but these and like things are said of Him by reason of His effects. For there follows: [[8:20|in the midst of the paths of judgment|in medio semitarum judicii]]. The paths of judgment are the precepts and ordinances, the laws and rules from which just judgments are given, or the acts of judgment with which God is well pleased; therefore He declares that He is in them and walks in them, in the way just mentioned.

paras.t: Ut ditem diligentes me, per abundantiam gratiæ ac virtutum in vita hac, et per copiam gloriæ in paradiso cœlesti, et thesauros eorum repleam, id est, merita eorum augeam in hoc mundo, et ea plenissime remunerem in futuro. Quamvis autem in veteri lege temporalium abundantia promittebatur justis ac diligentibus Deum, quod tamen illa non fuerit plena principalisque merces illorum, et quod de illa non loquatur hic Salomon, constat ex eo quod modo præmisit, Accipite disciplinam, et non pecuniam : quasi dicat, Temporalia principaliter non promitto : sicut expositum est. Præterea, de istis thesauris loquitur Filius Dei : Thesaurizate vobis thesauros in cœlo ; Apostolus quoque : Divitibus hujus sæculi præcipe thesaurizare sibi thesaurum bonum in futurum, ut apprehendant veram vitam, id est vitam gloriæ, in qua nulla est corruptio.
paras.en: [[8:21|That I may enrich them that love me|Ut ditem diligentes me]], by abundance of grace and virtues in this life and by plenty of glory in the heavenly paradise, [[8:21|and may fill their treasures|et thesauros eorum repleam]], that is, increase their merits in this world and reward them most fully in the world to come. And although in the old law an abundance of temporal things was promised to the just and to those who love God, yet that this was not their full and chief reward, and that Solomon is not speaking of it here, is clear from what he has just said before: [[8:10|Receive my instruction, and not money|Accipite disciplinam, et non pecuniam]]: as if to say, It is not chiefly temporal things that I promise, as has been explained. Besides, of these treasures the Son of God speaks: [[Matt 6:20|lay up to yourselves treasures in heaven|Thesaurizate vobis thesauros in cœlo]]; and the Apostle too: [[1 Tim 6:17|Charge the rich of this world|Divitibus hujus sæculi præcipe]] [[1 Tim 6:19|To lay up in store for themselves a good foundation against the time to come, that they may lay hold on the true life|thesaurizare sibi thesaurum bonum in futurum, ut apprehendant veram vitam]] [Denis has "a good treasure" for the Vulgate's "a good foundation"], that is, the life of glory, in which there is no corruption.

paras.t: Consequenter agit Salomon de generatione increatæ Sapientiæ, id est Verbi æterni, a Deo Patre : et tam evidenter super hoc loquitur, ut miranda, imo miseranda ac deploranda sit cæcitas atque perversitas negantium veram deitatem esse in Filio unico Dei Patris æterni. Dominus possedit me, id est, Pater æternus in corde et intellectu suo stabiliter et immobiliter habuit me : juxta illud, Unigenitus Filius qui est in sinu Patris ; in initio viarum suarum, id est ab exordio et in principio creaturarum operumque et mandatorum suorum : juxta illud, In principio erat Verbum. Porro creaturæ et mandata ac opera Dei, sunt viæ, quia sunt media pertingendi ad Creatoris notitiam, sicut scribit Apostolus : Invisibilia Dei, id est incomprehensibiles proprietates Dei, ejus videlicet omnipotentia, sapientia, benignitas, per ea quæ facta sunt, conspiciuntur. Unde et apud Job legitur, Ipse est principium viarum Dei : quod tamen ad litteram dicitur ibi de primo illo apostata angelo. Sicut enim effectus inducit ad suæ causæ cognitionem, sic creatura ad Creatoris notitiam. Similiter illuminationes ac jussiones, quas Deus ab initio impressit angelicis mentibus ac primis parentibus, fuerunt viæ ad Creatoris contemplationem, amorem et cultum.
paras.en: Next Solomon treats of the generation of the uncreated Wisdom, that is, of the eternal Word, from God the Father; and he speaks of it so plainly that the blindness and perversity of those who deny that true Godhead is in the only Son of the eternal God the Father is to be wondered at, nay, to be pitied and lamented. [[8:22|The Lord possessed me|Dominus possedit me]], that is, the eternal Father held me firmly and immovably in his heart and understanding, according to that saying: [[John 1:18|the only begotten Son who is in the Bosom of the Father|Unigenitus Filius qui est in sinu Patris]]; [[8:22|in the beginning of his ways|in initio viarum suarum]], that is, from the outset and in the beginning of his creatures, works and commandments, according to that saying: [[John 1:1|In the beginning was the Word|In principio erat Verbum]]. Now the creatures, commandments and works of God are *ways*, because they are means of attaining to the knowledge of the Creator, as the Apostle writes: [[Rom 1:20|the invisible things of him|Invisibilia Dei]], that is, the incomprehensible attributes of God, namely his omnipotence, wisdom and goodness, [[Rom 1:20|by the things that are made|per ea quæ facta sunt]], [[Rom 1:20|are clearly seen|conspiciuntur]]. Hence in Job too we read: [[Job 40:14|He is the beginning of the ways of God|Ipse est principium viarum Dei]]; though there, in the literal sense, it is said of that first apostate angel. For as an effect leads to the knowledge of its cause, so does the creature lead to the knowledge of the Creator. In the same way the illuminations and commands which God from the beginning imprinted on the minds of the angels and of our first parents were ways to the contemplation, love and worship of the Creator.

paras.t: Ne autem dicere quis auderet, Filium Dei fuisse quidem ab exordio mundi, sed non ante, imo cum aliis et inter alia esse creatum, subjungitur : Antequam quidquam faceret a principio. Verumtamen antiqua translatio habet, Dominus creavit me initio viarum suarum ; et ita allegat Ambrosius super psalmum, Beati immaculati. Dicuntque aliqui, quod creatio sumitur ibi extense, prout generationem includit. Alii dicunt, quod Sapientia dicitur ab initio esse creata, propter futurum tunc Incarnationis mysterium, in qua Verbum æternum factum est caro et homo, et quantum ad humanitatem, creatum. Unde et alio loco testatur : Ab initio et ante sæcula creata sum.
paras.en: But lest anyone should dare to say that the Son of God was indeed from the outset of the world, but not before it, nay, that he was created with other things and among them, there follows: [[8:22|before he made any thing from the beginning|Antequam quidquam faceret a principio]]. The old translation, however, has: *The Lord created me in the beginning of his ways*[[8:22||]] [the Old Latin version, made from the Greek Septuagint]; and so Ambrose cites it on the psalm *Beati immaculati*[[Ps 118:1||]] [that is, Psalm 118, "Blessed are the undefiled"]. And some say that *creation* is taken there in a wide sense, so as to include generation. Others say that Wisdom is said to have been created from the beginning because of the mystery of the Incarnation then to come, in which the eternal [[John 1:14|Word was made flesh|Verbum æternum factum est caro]] and man, and as to his humanity was created. Hence in another place too she testifies: [[Ecclus 24:14|From the beginning, and before the world, was I created|Ab initio et ante sæcula creata sum]].

paras.t: Insuper, ne impiissimus Arius et ejus sequaces affirmare ore blasphemo præsumant, Filium Dei esse creaturam, et tamen ante angelos ac mundum sensibilem esse creatum, non autem ab æterno, nec eum esse Patri coæternum, subjungitur : Ab æterno ordinata sum, id est æternaliter producta ac generata a Patre, ad producendum cum eo Spiritum Sanctum, manente ordine inter Patrem et me : ordine, inquam, naturæ et personalis distinctionis, non dignitatis aut temporis. Pater enim natura, id est naturali origine, prior est Filio, personaliterque distinctus ab eo; non autem dignitate aut tempore. Imo tres superbenedictæ et supergloriosæ ac adorandæ Personæ, sunt consubstantiales, coæquales et coæternæ. Et ex antiquis, scilicet exordiis temporum, imo et ante ea, et a diebus æternitatis. Unde Daniel Patrem æternum vocat, Antiquum dierum. Apostolus quoque ad Titum : Vitam, inquit, æternam promisit Deus ante tempora sæcularia. Hinc subditur : antequam terra fieret : de qua legitur, In principio creavit Deus cœlum et terram ; atque in Psalmo, Initio tu, Domine, terram fundasti. Vel spiritualiter, Antequam terra fieret, id est, priusquam Ecclesia formaretur.
paras.en: Moreover, lest the most impious Arius and his followers should presume to affirm with blasphemous mouth that the Son of God is a creature, created indeed before the angels and the visible world, yet not from eternity, and that he is not coeternal with the Father, there follows: [[8:23|I was set up from eternity|Ab æterno ordinata sum]] [*ordinata*, literally "ordered", "set in order": hence Denis goes on to speak of an *order*], that is, eternally brought forth and begotten of the Father, to bring forth with him the Holy Ghost, an order remaining between the Father and me: an order, I say, of nature and of personal distinction, not of dignity or of time. For the Father is prior to the Son by nature, that is, by natural origin, and personally distinct from him; but not by dignity or by time. Nay, the three superblessed, superglorious and adorable Persons are consubstantial, coequal and coeternal. [[8:23|and of old|Et ex antiquis]], namely from the first beginnings of the times, nay, even before them, and from the days of eternity. Hence Daniel calls the eternal Father [[Dan 7:9|the ancient of days|Antiquum dierum]] [the margin gives Dan. vii, 9, 13, 22: the title stands in all three verses]. The Apostle too, to Titus: [[Tit 1:2|life|Vitam]], he says, [[Tit 1:2|everlasting, which God, who lieth not, hath promised before the times of the world|æternam promisit Deus ante tempora sæcularia]]. Hence there follows: [[8:23|before the earth was made|antequam terra fieret]]: of which we read: [[Gen 1:1|In the beginning God created heaven, and earth|In principio creavit Deus cœlum et terram]]; and in the Psalm: [[Ps 101:26|In the beginning, O Lord, thou foundedst the earth|Initio tu, Domine, terram fundasti]]. Or spiritually: [[8:23|before the earth was made|Antequam terra fieret]], that is, before the Church was formed.

paras.t: Nondum erant abyssi, id est maria, et ego jam concepta eram, id est genita. In simplicissimo enim Deo, idem est concipere et gignere, quia non aliunde concipit Pater, sicut in carnali generatione mater concipit a patre seu viro. Pater autem æternus se ipsum æternaliter ac superplenissime et invariabiliter intuendo ac intelligendo, id quod in se intuetur atque intelligit, hoc in se concipit, profert seu gignit : et hoc est Verbum ejus æternum, perfecta et plena ac naturalis imago Patris genita, et infinita sapientia ejus : in quo Verbo æterno plenissime, quidquid Patris est, resplendet. Nondum fontes aquarum eruperant originaliter de Oceano per subterranea loca, et de occultis receptaculis ac ventriculis suis sub terra latentibus.
paras.en: [[8:24|The depths were not as yet|Nondum erant abyssi]], that is, the seas, [[8:24|and I was already conceived|et ego jam concepta eram]], that is, begotten. For in God, who is utterly simple, to conceive and to beget are the same, since the Father does not conceive from another, as in carnal generation the mother conceives from the father or husband. But the eternal Father, beholding and understanding himself eternally, most superabundantly and unchangeably, conceives, utters or begets in himself that which he beholds and understands in himself: and this is his eternal Word, the begotten, perfect, full and natural image of the Father, and his infinite wisdom[[1 Cor 1:24||]]; in which eternal Word whatever is the Father's shines forth most fully. [[8:24|neither had the fountains of waters as yet sprung out|Nondum fontes aquarum eruperant]], at their origin, from the Ocean through places under the earth, and from their hidden reservoirs and chambers lying concealed beneath the earth.

paras.t: Nondum montes gravi mole, id est magnitudine, constiterant elevati super planitiem terræ. Ante colles ego parturiebar.
paras.en: [[8:25|The mountains, with their huge bulk|Nondum montes gravi mole]], that is, size, [[8:25|had not as yet been established|constiterant]], raised up above the plain of the earth. [[8:25|before the hills, I was brought forth|Ante colles ego parturiebar]].

paras.t: Adhuc terram non fecerat, et flumina, et cardines orbis terræ. Per cardines, possunt extremitates terræ intelligi, vel duæ extremitates axis, circa quas circumfertur cœlum, sicut janua ad cardines suos : quæ extremitates sunt polus arcticus atque antarcticus. Vel, cardines orbis terræ, sunt quatuor principales terræ partes, oriens, occidens, auster et aquilo.
paras.en: [[8:26|He had not yet made the earth, nor the rivers, nor the poles of the world.|Adhuc terram non fecerat, et flumina, et cardines orbis terræ.]] By the *poles* [*cardines*, literally "hinges"] may be understood the extremities of the earth, or the two ends of the axis about which the heaven turns, as a door turns on its hinges: and these ends are the arctic and the antarctic pole. Or the [[8:26|poles of the world|cardines orbis terræ]] are the four principal parts of the earth: east, west, south and north.

paras.t: Quando præparabat cælos, aderam : id est, quando cœlestes orbes creavit, et creando ad commoda hominum ordinavit, adfui. Quando certa lege et gyro vallabat abyssos, id est, aquis Oceani per circuitum præfixit quousque extenderent se, et moverentur versus terram. Unde loquitur Deus beato Job : Quis conclusit ostiis mare, quando erumpebat quasi de vulva procedens ? Circumdedi illud terminis meis, et posui vectem et ostia, et dixi : Hucusque venies, et non procedes amplius, et hic confringes tumentes fluctus tuos. Ideo ait Psalmista de Deo : Congregans sicut in utre aquas maris, ponens in thesauris abyssos.
paras.en: [[8:27|When he prepared the heavens, I was present|Quando præparabat cælos, aderam]]: that is, when he created the heavenly spheres, and in creating them ordered them to the benefit of men, I was there. [[8:27|when with a certain law, and compass, he enclosed the depths|Quando certa lege et gyro vallabat abyssos]], that is, he fixed for the waters of the Ocean round about how far they should spread and move toward the land. Hence God speaks to blessed Job: [[Job 38:8|Who shut up the sea with doors, when it broke forth as issuing out of the womb:|Quis conclusit ostiis mare, quando erumpebat quasi de vulva procedens]] [[Job 38:10|I set my bounds around it, and made it bars and doors:|Circumdedi illud terminis meis, et posui vectem et ostia]] [[Job 38:11|And I said: Hitherto thou shalt come, and shalt go no further, and here thou shalt break thy swelling waves.|et dixi : Hucusque venies, et non procedes amplius, et hic confringes tumentes fluctus tuos]] Therefore the Psalmist says of God: [[Ps 32:7|Gathering together the waters of the sea, as in a vessel; laying up the depths in storehouses.|Congregans sicut in utre aquas maris, ponens in thesauris abyssos]]

paras.t: Quando æthera, id est sphæram ignis proximam lunæ, vel superiorem aeris regionem, firmabat sursum, id est, firmiter collocavit in apice elementorum ; et librabat, id est, in pondere et in mensura sua constituit, fontes aquarum. Hæc enim et consimilia sunt opera Creatoris : de quo legitur in Isaia, Quis libravit in pondere montes, et colles in statera ?
paras.en: [[8:28|When he established the sky|Quando æthera]], that is, the sphere of fire nearest the moon, or the upper region of the air, [[8:28|above|firmabat sursum]], that is, set it firmly at the summit of the elements; [[8:28|and poised|et librabat]], that is, set in their weight and measure, [[8:28|the fountains of waters|fontes aquarum]]. For these and the like are the works of the Creator, of whom we read in Isaias: Who hath [[Is 40:12|weighed the mountains in scales, and the hills in a balance?|libravit in pondere montes, et colles in statera]]

paras.t: Quando circumdabat mari terminum suum : qui terminus communiter est terra mollis et arenosa : sicque in hoc declaratur omnipotentia summi opificis, ex cujus præcepto mare frenatur, ne tam debilem exeat terminum. Ex quo possumus contemplari quam metuendus sit Deus. Propter quod nos per Jeremiam hortatur : Audi, popule stulte, qui non habes cor : Me non timebitis, qui posui arenam terminum maris, præceptum sempiternum, quod non præteribit ? Intumescent fluctus ejus, et non transibunt illud. Hinc subditur : et legem, id est præceptum seu ordinationem, ponebat aquis, ne transirent fines suos. Voluit enim Omnipotens partem terræ esse discoopertam ab aquis, propter hominum et animalium habitationem ac sustentationem. Aqua autem ex sua natura, quum sit subtilior ac levior terra, inclinaretur terram ascendere, nisi Creatoris restringeretur præcepto : quod tamen naturale atque conveniens est respectu universalis naturæ, quemadmodum et descensus ignis in generatione mixtorum. Quando appendebat fundamenta terræ, id est, in medio universi creavit ac statuit elementum terræ, et partes ejus inferiores ac interiores circa centrum, quæ fundamentum videntur partium aliarum. Unde Dominus ait ad Job : Ubi eras, quando ponebam fundamenta terræ ? Super quo bases ejus solidatæ sunt ?
paras.en: [[8:29|When he compassed the sea with its bounds|Quando circumdabat mari terminum suum]]: which bound is commonly soft and sandy ground; and so in this is shown the omnipotence of the supreme Maker, at whose command the sea is bridled so that it does not pass so weak a bound. From this we may consider how greatly God is to be feared. Wherefore he exhorts us by Jeremias: [[Jer 5:21|Hear, O foolish people, and without understanding|Audi, popule stulte, qui non habes cor]]: [[Jer 5:22|Will not you then fear me|Me non timebitis]], who [[Jer 5:22|have set the sand a bound for the sea, an everlasting ordinance, which it shall not pass over|posui arenam terminum maris, præceptum sempiternum, quod non præteribit]]? [[Jer 5:22|they shall swell, and shall not pass over it|Intumescent fluctus ejus, et non transibunt illud]]. Hence there follows: [[8:29|and set a law|et legem]], that is, a command or ordinance, [[8:29|to the waters that they should not pass their limits|ponebat aquis, ne transirent fines suos]]. For the Almighty willed that part of the earth should be left uncovered by the waters, for the dwelling and sustenance of men and animals. But water, being by its nature finer and lighter than earth, would tend to rise over the earth, were it not held back by the Creator's command; which is nevertheless natural and fitting with respect to universal nature, as is also the descent of fire in the generation of mixed bodies [in the physics of the schools each element tends to its own place, fire upward, yet the order of the whole draws fire down into compound bodies; so too the waters are held back from their own place for the good of the whole]. [[8:29|when he balanced the foundations of the earth|Quando appendebat fundamenta terræ]], that is, he created and set the element of earth in the middle of the universe, and its lower and inner parts about the centre, which seem to be the foundation of the other parts. Hence the Lord says to Job: [[Job 38:4|Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth?|Ubi eras, quando ponebam fundamenta terræ]] [[Job 38:6|Upon what are its bases grounded?|Super quo bases ejus solidatæ sunt]]

paras.t: Cum eo eram cuncta componens, id est producens et ordinans : nam sicut superessentialis et superfelicissimæ Trinitatis est una natura et una potestas, ita operatio una ad extra, ejusque opera sunt indivisa. Ideo scriptum est : Quæcumque facit Pater, hæc et Filius similiter facit. Et delectabar per singulos dies. Infinita est enim beatitudo et gaudium uniuscujusque increatæ et adorandæ Personæ, et cum jucunditate intensive immensa intuentur, diligunt et fruuntur se invicem. Ludens, id est delectabiliter agens ac operans, coram eo omni tempore : juxta illud in Psalmo, Lætabitur Dominus in operibus suis. Unde Unigenitus ait : Pater meus usque modo operatur, et ego operor.
paras.en: [[8:30|I was with him forming all things|Cum eo eram cuncta componens]], that is, bringing forth and ordering: for as the superessential and most superblessed Trinity has one nature and one power, so it has one operation *ad extra* [that is, in what it does outside itself, in creatures], and its works are undivided. Therefore it is written: [[John 5:19|what things soever he doth, these the Son also doth in like manner|Quæcumque facit Pater, hæc et Filius similiter facit]]. [[8:30|and was delighted every day|Et delectabar per singulos dies]]. For infinite is the beatitude and joy of each of the uncreated and adorable Persons, and with a delight intensively immeasurable they behold, love and enjoy one another. [[8:30|playing|Ludens]], that is, acting and working with delight, [[8:30|before him at all times|coram eo omni tempore]]: according to that in the Psalm: [[Ps 103:31|the Lord shall rejoice in his works|Lætabitur Dominus in operibus suis]]. Hence the Only-begotten says: [[John 5:17|My Father worketh until now; and I work|Pater meus usque modo operatur, et ego operor]].

paras.t: Ludens in orbe terrarum, id est deliciose disponens quæ fiunt in eo ex fonte providentiæ meæ. Vel ideo ait, Ludens in orbe terrarum, quoniam ea quæ operatur in terra, sunt quasi ludus respectu supernaturalium, divinorum, cœlestiumque suorum effectuum ; vel, quoniam sicut is qui ludit cum pila, percutit eam de loco ad locum, sic increata Sapientia variat mundi statum, et transfert regna de gente in gentem, et excutit iniquos de loco suo ad alium, prout inducitur : Opus manuum ejus sunt universi; subito morientur. Conteret multos et innumerabiles, et stare faciet alios pro eis; quasi impios percussit eos in loco videntium.
paras.en: [[8:31|Playing in the world|Ludens in orbe terrarum]], that is, delightfully disposing the things that come to pass in it from the fountain of my providence. Or he says [[8:31|Playing in the world|Ludens in orbe terrarum]] because the things that Wisdom works on earth are as it were a game compared with her supernatural, divine and heavenly effects; or because, as one who plays with a ball strikes it from place to place, so the uncreated Wisdom changes the state of the world, transfers kingdoms from nation to nation, and drives the wicked out of their place to another, as is said [in Job]: [[Job 34:19|all are the work of his hands|Opus manuum ejus sunt universi]]; [[Job 34:20|They shall suddenly die|subito morientur]]. [[Job 34:24|He shall break in pieces many and innumerable, and shall make others to stand in their stead.|Conteret multos et innumerabiles, et stare faciet alios pro eis]] [[Job 34:26|He hath struck them, as being wicked, in open sight.|quasi impios percussit eos in loco videntium]]

paras.t: Et deliciæ meæ, esse cum filiis hominum. Ecce quam dulce verbum est hoc. Etenim beneplacitum est Domino in populo suo : de quo ait per Jeremiam, Lætabor super eis quum benefecero ipsis. Itaque, Deliciæ meæ, esse cum filiis hominum, id est, valde delectabile mihi est, inter justos et virtuosos per gratiam commorari, et in eorum amore quiescere, ac laudabilia eorum exercitia intueri. Nempe quo fragiliores sunt per naturam, eo in eorum conatu ad perficiendum, et in pugna eorum contra invisibiles hostes ac aciem vitiorum, magis delector. Videtur quoque increata Sapientia istud dixisse, propter Incarnationis mysterium, quo assumptura erat naturam humanam, et inter homines conversatura ex nimia sua caritate ad genus humanum. Denique in rebus et creaturis irrationabilibus ac animatis, est Deus per essentiam, præsentiam et potentiam, non autem per caritatem et gratiam. Ideo respectu existentiæ qua in illis est, deliciosum sibi est esse cum filiis hominum, in quibus per gratiam et caritatem existit. Verumtamen non est putandum, quod aliquid delectationis accrescat Deo ex creaturis, vel ex consistentia ejus cum hominibus ; sed quoniam in se ipso tam bonus, amorosus et pius est, ideo deliciosum sibi est tam dignanter ad homines se habere.
paras.en: [[8:31|and my delights were to be with the children of men|Et deliciæ meæ, esse cum filiis hominum]]. Behold how sweet a word this is. For [[Ps 149:4|the Lord is well pleased with his people|beneplacitum est Domino in populo suo]]; of whom he says by Jeremias: [[Jer 32:41|I will rejoice over them, when I shall do them good|Lætabor super eis quum benefecero ipsis]]. And so, [[8:31|my delights were to be with the children of men|Deliciæ meæ, esse cum filiis hominum]]: that is, it is very delightful to me to dwell by grace among the just and virtuous, to rest in their love, and to behold their praiseworthy exercises. For the frailer they are by nature, the more I delight in their striving after perfection, and in their fight against the invisible enemies and the battle-line of the vices. The uncreated Wisdom seems also to have said this because of the mystery of the Incarnation, by which she was to take human nature and to converse among men[[Bar 3:38||]] out of her exceeding charity toward the human race. Again, in things and creatures without reason, even living ones, God is by essence, presence and power, but not by charity and grace [the schoolmen's formula: God is in all things by his essence, as giving them being; by his presence, as seeing all; by his power, as all being subject to it; in the just he dwells also by grace]. Therefore, compared with the way in which he exists in them, it is delightful to him to be with the children of men, in whom he dwells by grace and charity. Yet it is not to be thought that any delight accrues to God from creatures, or from his abiding with men; but because in himself he is so good, loving and kind, therefore it is delightful to him to bear himself so graciously toward men.

paras.t: Sint ergo et nostræ deliciæ esse cum ipso, adhæreamusque ei indesinenter, amando, contemplando, laudando, orando, omnique modo nobis possibili vicem suæ dignationi piissimæ exhibendo. Et certe væ eis qui ei ingrati sunt, et mentem suam ab eo avertunt, qui in tantum nos diligit, quod etiam in Sacramento semper nobiscum est, et in illo se præstat nobis.
paras.en: Let it be our delight too, then, to be with him; and let us cleave to him unceasingly, loving, contemplating, praising, praying, and in every way possible to us making return for his most loving condescension. And surely woe to those who are ungrateful to him and turn their mind away from him, who loves us so much that he is always with us even in the Sacrament, and gives himself to us in it.

paras.t: Hinc increata Sapientia consequenter hortatur. Nunc ergo, filii, audite me : Beati nunc in spe et merito, qui custodiunt vias meas, id est divina præcepta. Audite disciplinam, et estote sapientes, et nolite abjicere eam : quoniam sine dono sapientiæ nemo potest salvari, sicut nec sine caritate ; et neminem diligit Deus, nisi qui cum sapientia inhabitat.
paras.en: Hence the uncreated Wisdom goes on to exhort: [[8:32|Now, therefore, ye children, hear me|Nunc ergo, filii, audite me]]: [[8:32|blessed|Beati]], now in hope and merit, [[8:32|are they that keep my ways|qui custodiunt vias meas]], that is, the divine commandments. [[8:33|Hear instruction, and be wise, and refuse it not|Audite disciplinam, et estote sapientes, et nolite abjicere eam]]: for without the gift of wisdom no one can be saved, as neither without charity; and [[Wis 7:28|God loveth none but him that dwelleth with wisdom|neminem diligit Deus, nisi qui cum sapientia inhabitat]].

paras.t: Beatus homo qui audit me aure obeditionis, qui vigilat ad fores meas quotidie, id est, sacra loca divini cultus ac prædicationis assidue visitat cum vigilantia mentis devotæ ; et observat ad postes ostii mei, id est, attendit verba doctorum ac Scripturarum, per quæ intratur in domum Dei, in Ecclesiam militantem, ac triumphantem.
paras.en: [[8:34|Blessed is the man that heareth me|Beatus homo qui audit me]] with the ear of obedience, [[8:34|and that watcheth daily at my gates|qui vigilat ad fores meas quotidie]], that is, who diligently visits the holy places of divine worship and of preaching with the watchfulness of a devout mind; [[8:34|and waiteth at the posts of my doors|et observat ad postes ostii mei]], that is, who attends to the words of the doctors and of the Scriptures, through which one enters into the house of God, into the Church militant and triumphant.

paras.t: Qui me invenerit, id est, cor suum mihi unierit per fidem et obedientiam, inveniet vitam vere virtuosam, ac gloriam æternalem : ego enim sum via, veritas et vita ; et hauriet salutem a Domino, id est, felicitatem æternam a fonte totius beatitudinis sortietur. Qui autem peccaverit in me, per transgressionem præcepti, lædet animam suam, id est, sibi ipsi, non mihi, nocebit : et ipsum peccatum, est læsio atque interitus animæ. Sed et veniale peccatum animam peccantis aliqualiter lædit, non tamen letaliter, sed ad letalem læsionem disponit, imo et cito ad eam perducet, nisi quotidie refrenetur ac castigetur : quia hoc facit sentina neglecta, quod fluctus irruens.
paras.en: [[8:35|He that shall find me|Qui me invenerit]], that is, shall have united his heart to me by faith and obedience, [[8:35|shall find life|inveniet vitam]] truly virtuous, and eternal glory: for [[John 14:6|I am the way, and the truth, and the life|ego enim sum via, veritas et vita]]; [[8:35|and shall have salvation from the Lord|et hauriet salutem a Domino]] [*hauriet*, literally "shall draw", as water from a spring], that is, he shall obtain eternal happiness from the fountain of all beatitude. [[8:36|But he that shall sin against me|Qui autem peccaverit in me]], by transgressing the commandment, [[8:36|shall hurt his own soul|lædet animam suam]], that is, he will harm himself, not me: and sin itself is the hurt and the death of the soul. But venial sin too hurts the soul of the sinner in some measure, not mortally indeed, yet it disposes to mortal hurt, nay, will soon bring the soul to it, unless it is checked and chastised daily: for a neglected bilge does what a breaking wave does [that is, water left to gather in the hold sinks a ship as surely as a wave breaking over it].

paras.t: Omnes qui me oderunt : vel ipsam Sapientiam increatam in se ipsa detestando ac odiendo : quod est formaliter ac proprie Deum odire, et non nisi impiissimis convenit; vel ejus præcepta parvi pendendo, et mentem avertendo a summo bono : quod plurimi faciunt : diligunt mortem, id est, ita se habent, ac si mortem animæ miseriamque gehennæ amarent, faciendo ea per quæ quotidie propinquant ad mortem. Diligunt quoque mortem, id est opera vitiosa et peccata, quæ sunt mors animæ. Unde scriptum est : Injustitia mortis est acquisitio : impii autem manibus et verbis arcessierunt illam.
paras.en: [[8:36|All that hate me|Omnes qui me oderunt]], either by detesting and hating the uncreated Wisdom herself in herself, which is formally and properly to hate God, and befits none but the most impious; or by making light of her commandments and turning the mind away from the supreme good, which very many do: [[8:36|love death|diligunt mortem]], that is, they behave as if they loved the death of the soul and the misery of hell, doing the things by which they daily draw nearer to death. They also [[8:36|love death|Diligunt quoque mortem]], that is, vicious works and sins, which are the death of the soul. Hence it is written: Injustice is the acquiring of death [these words stand after Wis 1:15 in some older copies of the Vulgate; they are not in the Clementine text or the Douay-Rheims]: [[Wis 1:16|But the wicked with works and words have called it to them|impii autem manibus et verbis arcessierunt illam]].

9.title: DECLARATIO CAPITULI NONI : SAPIENTIA ÆDIFICAVIT SIBI DOMUM.
9.title_en: Declaration of the ninth chapter: Wisdom hath built herself a house.

paras.t: Capitulo præcedenti egit Salomon de æterna generatione, veraque deitate unigeniti Filii Dei. Hic agit de ejus incarnatione, ejusque humanitatis mysteriis.
paras.en: In the preceding chapter Solomon treated of the eternal generation and true Godhead of the only-begotten Son of God. Here he treats of His incarnation, and of the mysteries of His humanity.

paras.t: Sapientia increata, de qua in præcedenti capitulo dictum est, ædificavit sibi domum, id est corpus, quod formavit et assumpsit ex purissimis Virginis sacræ sanguinibus. Vel, Domum, id est assumptam humanitatem, in qua tanquam in domo habitavit : de qua dixit Judæis, Solvite templum hoc. Rursus domus hæc, potest dici Ecclesia : de qua ad Hebræos ait Apostolus, Christus tanquam Filius in domo sua ; atque ad Timotheum, Scias quomodo oporteat te conversari in domo Dei, quæ est Ecclesia Dei vivi : quam ædificavit Salvator, legem evangelicam cum suis sacramentis instituendo, et homines ad fidem catholicam convertendo. Unde dixit ad beatissimum Petrum : Tu es Petrus, et super hanc petram ædificabo Ecclesiam meam. Ædificavit eam verbo instructionis, et conversatione exemplari ac sancta, quemadmodum scriptum est : Cœpit Jesus facere et docere.
paras.en: [[9:1|Wisdom|Sapientia]] uncreated, of whom the preceding chapter spoke, [[9:1|hath built herself a house|ædificavit sibi domum]], that is, the body which she formed and assumed from the most pure blood of the holy Virgin. Or, [[9:1|a house|Domum]], that is, the humanity assumed, in which she dwelt as in a house: of which He said to the Jews, [[John 2:19|Destroy this temple|Solvite templum hoc]]. Again, this house can be called the Church: of which the Apostle says to the Hebrews, [[Heb 3:6|Christ, as the Son in his own house|Christus tanquam Filius in domo sua]]; and to Timothy, [[1 Tim 3:15|thou mayest know how thou oughtest to behave thyself in the house of God, which is the church of the living God|Scias quomodo oporteat te conversari in domo Dei, quæ est Ecclesia Dei vivi]]: which the Saviour built by instituting the law of the Gospel with its sacraments, and by converting men to the Catholic faith. Hence He said to the most blessed Peter: [[Matt 16:18|thou art Peter; and upon this rock I will build my church|Tu es Petrus, et super hanc petram ædificabo Ecclesiam meam]]. He built it by the word of instruction and by an exemplary and holy way of life, as it is written: [[Acts 1:1|Jesus began to do and to teach|Cœpit Jesus facere et docere]].

paras.t: Excidit columnas septem. Columnæ septem sustentantes domum præfactam, sunt septem sacramenta, vel septem dona : quæ etiam in Christi anima plenissime erant et sunt, et ejus Ecclesiam stabiliunt ac decorant. Rursus, quia, ut dictum est, septenario designatur totalitas atque perfectio, possunt per septem columnas intelligi universæ particulares Ecclesiæ per orbem diffusæ, quæ significatæ sunt per septem Ecclesias Asiæ, quibus in Apocalypsi scripsit S. Joannes. Nam et ipsam Ecclesiam vocat Apostolus columnam et firmamentum veritatis. Similiter universitas Apostolorum et apostolicorum virorum, qui sua sanctitate et doctrina et exemplaritate instituerunt ac fundaverunt Ecclesiam, possunt per septem columnas signari : sicut de Petro, Jacobo et Joanne scribit Paulus, quod videbantur columnæ esse. Has Salvator excidit, id est, de mundo per gratiam suam abstraxit, spiritualiterque ornavit.
paras.en: [[9:1|she hath hewn her out seven pillars|Excidit columnas septem]]. The seven pillars holding up the aforesaid house are the seven sacraments, or the seven gifts [that is, of the Holy Ghost]: which were and are most fully in the soul of Christ, and which make His Church firm and adorn it. Again, since, as has been said, the number seven signifies totality and perfection, the seven pillars can be understood as all the particular Churches spread throughout the world, which were signified by the seven Churches of Asia to which St. John wrote in the Apocalypse[[Apoc 1:4||]][[Apoc 2:1||]][[Apoc 3:1||]]. For the Apostle calls the Church itself [[1 Tim 3:15|the pillar and ground of the truth|columnam et firmamentum veritatis]]. Likewise the whole company of the Apostles and apostolic men, who by their holiness, teaching and example established and founded the Church, can be signified by the seven pillars: as Paul writes of Peter, James and John, that they [[Gal 2:9|seemed to be pillars|videbantur columnæ esse]]. These the Saviour hewed out, that is, drew out of the world by His grace, and adorned spiritually.

paras.t: Immolavit victimas suas. Christus namque spirituales hostias, scilicet sacrificium laudis, orationem et gratiarum actionem, promptissimamque obedientiam secundum assumptam humanitatem obtulit Deo Patri, imo toti superexcellentissimæ Trinitati ; et tandem obtulit se ipsum in cruce oblationem et hostiam Deo in odorem suavitatis. Sicque obtulit victimas, id est corpus suum et sanguinem. Unde fuit prædictum : Oblatus est, quia voluit. Miscuit vinum : nam in Cœna novissima vinum convertit in sanguinem suum ; et ut Thomas ac alii multi testantur, probabile est quod vinum illud fuit lymphatum, id est aqua mixtum, quia in terra promissionis sunt fortia vina. Miscuit quoque vinum spirituale, id est arduam et exhilarativam, imo et spiritualiter inebriativam doctrinam, in sermone quem fecit post Cœnam. Et proposuit mensam suam, id est evangelicam legem, in qua omnium internorum ferculorum copia continetur, et Eucharistiæ communionem, quam dedit in Cœna. Jussit etiam mensam corporalem parari, dicendo discipulis : Euntes parate nobis pascha, ut manducemus. Promisit quoque tunc mensam cœlestis convivii, dicens : Ego dispono vobis regnum, ut edatis et bibatis super mensam meam in regno meo.
paras.en: [[9:2|She hath slain her victims|Immolavit victimas suas]]. For Christ, according to the humanity He assumed, offered spiritual sacrifices to God the Father, nay, to the whole most supremely excellent Trinity: namely the sacrifice of praise, prayer and thanksgiving, and the most ready obedience; and at last He offered Himself on the cross, [[Eph 5:2|an oblation and a sacrifice to God for an odour of sweetness|oblationem et hostiam Deo in odorem suavitatis]]. And so He offered victims, that is, His body and blood. Hence it was foretold: [[Is 53:7|He was offered because it was his own will|Oblatus est, quia voluit]]. [[9:2|mingled her wine|Miscuit vinum]]: for at the Last Supper He changed wine into His blood[[Matt 26:27||]] [the margin gives Matt. xxvi, 27; the words of consecration over the chalice are in the next verse, Matt 26:28]; and, as Thomas and many others testify, it is probable that that wine was watered, that is, mixed with water, because in the land of promise the wines are strong. She [[9:2|mingled|Miscuit]] also a spiritual wine, that is, a lofty and gladdening, nay, a spiritually inebriating doctrine, in the discourse which He gave after the Supper. [[9:2|and set forth her table|Et proposuit mensam suam]], that is, the law of the Gospel, in which is contained an abundance of all inward dishes, and the communion of the Eucharist, which He gave at the Supper. He also ordered a bodily table to be prepared, saying to the disciples: [[Luke 22:8|Go, and prepare for us the pasch, that we may eat|Euntes parate nobis pascha, ut manducemus]]. He then also promised the table of the heavenly banquet, saying: [[Luke 22:29|And I dispose to you|Ego dispono vobis]] [[Luke 22:29|a kingdom|regnum]], [[Luke 22:30|That you may eat and drink at my table, in my kingdom|ut edatis et bibatis super mensam meam in regno meo]].

paras.t: Misit ancillas suas, id est prædicatorum suorum collectiones, præsertim gloriosos Apostolos, qui ob sui obsequii promptissimi assiduitatem humillimam, recte vocantur ancillæ. Sunt et quidam Hebræi doctores, qui per domum sapientiæ, intelligunt Synagogam ; per ancillas, intelligunt Moysen et Aaron. Ut vocarent ad arcem, id est, ut ipsos quibus prædicare missi erant, invitarent ad altitudinem evangelicæ legis ac fidei, ad apicem regni cœlestis, ad verticem virtuosæ perfectionis ; et ad mœnia civitatis. Civitas ista est Ecclesia militans : de qua in Psalmo prædicatur, Gloriosa dicta sunt de te, civitas Dei ; et rursum alibi, Civitatem sanctam calcabunt mensibus quadraginta duobus. De qua alibi fertur : Accessistis ad montem Sion, et civitatem Dei viventis. Mœnia civitatis istius, sunt divina subsidia, angelicæ quoque custodiæ, virtuosi prælati, et ea quibus fides catholica roboratur : quibus omnibus munitur et circumvallatur Ecclesia tanquam fortissimis muris. Imo de Christo et ejus Ecclesia scriptum est : Urbs fortitudinis nostræ Sion ; Salvator ponetur in ea murus et antemurale. Ad hæc mœnia vocantur fideles, ut intra ea confugiant, protegantur atque salventur, innitendo divinis subsidiis, et angelorum custodiis ac prælatorum doctrinis. A quibus non exeant, quemadmodum de quibusdam asseritur : Ex nobis prodierunt, sed non erant ex nobis : nam si fuissent ex nobis, mansissent utique nobiscum.
paras.en: [[9:3|She hath sent her maids|Misit ancillas suas]], that is, the companies of her preachers, above all the glorious Apostles, who for the most humble constancy of their most ready service are rightly called maids. There are also certain Hebrew doctors who understand by the house of wisdom the Synagogue, and by the maids Moses and Aaron. [[9:3|to invite to the tower|Ut vocarent ad arcem]], that is, to invite those to whom they were sent to preach to the height of the law and faith of the Gospel, to the summit of the heavenly kingdom, to the peak of virtuous perfection; [[9:3|and to the walls of the city|et ad mœnia civitatis]]. That city is the Church militant: of which it is proclaimed in the Psalm, [[Ps 86:3|Glorious things are said of thee, O city of God|Gloriosa dicta sunt de te, civitas Dei]]; and again elsewhere, [[Apoc 11:2|the holy city they shall tread under foot, two and forty months|Civitatem sanctam calcabunt mensibus quadraginta duobus]]. Of which it is said elsewhere: [[Heb 12:22|you are come to mount Sion and to the city of the living God|Accessistis ad montem Sion, et civitatem Dei viventis]]. The walls of that city are the divine helps, and also the guardianship of the angels, virtuous prelates, and the things by which the Catholic faith is strengthened: by all of which the Church is fortified and encircled as by the strongest walls. Nay, of Christ and His Church it is written: [[Is 26:1|Sion the city of our strength a saviour, a wall and a bulwark shall be set therein|Urbs fortitudinis nostræ Sion ; Salvator ponetur in ea murus et antemurale]]. To these walls the faithful are called, so that they may flee within them and be protected and saved, relying on the divine helps, and on the guardianship of the angels and the teachings of the prelates. And let them not go out from these, as is said of certain men: [[1 John 2:19|They went out from us but they were not of us. For if they had been of us, they would no doubt have remained with us|Ex nobis prodierunt, sed non erant ex nobis : nam si fuissent ex nobis, mansissent utique nobiscum]].

paras.t: Si quis est parvulus, id est pauper, vilis et modicus in oculis suis, hoc est humilis, veniat ad me. Humiles quippe, ad divinæ sapientiæ susceptionem ac alia gratiarum charismata magis dispositi sunt, juxta illud Psalmi : Testimonium Domini fidele, sapientiam præstans parvulis ; itemque, Declaratio sermonum tuorum illuminat, et intellectum dat parvulis. Super hoc gavisus est Christus, Sapientia æternalis, secundum quod dicit Evangelista : Exsultavit Jesus Spiritu Sancto, et dixit : Confiteor tibi, Pater, Domine cœli et terræ, quoniam abscondisti hæc a sapientibus et prudentibus, et revelasti ea parvulis. Sed quia Salvator non solum vocavit humiles, imo etiam universos errantes, sicut in Evangelio protestatur, Venit Filius hominis quærere et salvare quod perierat ; recte subjungitur :
paras.en: [[9:4|Whosoever is a little one|Si quis est parvulus]], that is, poor, mean and small in his own eyes, that is, humble, [[9:4|let him come to me|veniat ad me]]. For the humble are better disposed to receive divine wisdom and the other gifts of grace, according to that of the Psalm: [[Ps 18:8|the testimony of the Lord is faithful, giving wisdom to little ones|Testimonium Domini fidele, sapientiam præstans parvulis]]; and likewise, [[Ps 118:130|The declaration of thy words giveth light: and giveth understanding to little ones.|Declaratio sermonum tuorum illuminat, et intellectum dat parvulis]] Over this Christ, the eternal Wisdom, rejoiced, as the Evangelist says: Jesus [[Luke 10:21|rejoiced in the Holy Ghost and said: I confess to thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because thou hast hidden these things from the wise and prudent and hast revealed them to little ones|Exsultavit Jesus Spiritu Sancto, et dixit : Confiteor tibi, Pater, Domine cœli et terræ, quoniam abscondisti hæc a sapientibus et prudentibus, et revelasti ea parvulis]]. But since the Saviour called not only the humble but also all who go astray, as He declares in the Gospel, [[Luke 19:10|the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost|Venit Filius hominis quærere et salvare quod perierat]], it is rightly added:

paras.t: Et insipientibus locuta est : insipientes namque sunt, universi qui carnalia et caduca præferunt summo et incommutabili bono. Venite per mentis conversionem, comedite panem meum, id est corpus meum in Sacramento, de quo dixi, Caro mea vere est cibus ; panem quoque lacrimarum, per veram contritionem ; panem vitæ et intellectus, per contemplationem ; panem obedientiæ, per præceptorum impletionem. Unde ait Salvator : Meus cibus est, ut faciam voluntatem Patris mei. Et certe omnia ista optime mentem reficiunt, roborant, impinguant. Et bibite vinum quod miscui vobis, hoc est sanguinem, seu præfatam doctrinam. Unde testatus sum : Sanguis meus vere est potus. De hoc pane et vino Zacharias ait : Quid bonum Domini, et quid pulchrum ejus, nisi frumentum electorum, et vinum germinans virgines ?
paras.en: [[9:4|And to the unwise she said|Et insipientibus locuta est]]: for the unwise are all those who prefer carnal and perishable things to the highest and unchangeable good. [[9:5|Come|Venite]] by conversion of mind, [[9:5|eat my bread|comedite panem meum]], that is, my body in the Sacrament, of which I said, [[John 6:56|my flesh is meat indeed|Caro mea vere est cibus]]; and also the bread of tears, by true contrition; the bread of life and understanding, by contemplation; the bread of obedience, by the fulfilling of the commandments. Hence the Saviour says: [[John 4:34|My meat is to do the will|Meus cibus est, ut faciam voluntatem]] of my Father [the Gospel reads "of him that sent me"]. And surely all these refresh, strengthen and fatten the mind excellently. [[9:5|and drink the wine which I have mingled for you|Et bibite vinum quod miscui vobis]], that is, my blood, or the doctrine spoken of above. Hence I testified: [[John 6:56|my blood is drink indeed|Sanguis meus vere est potus]]. Of this bread and wine Zacharias says: [[Zach 9:17|what is the good thing of him, and what is his beautiful thing, but the corn of the elect, and wine springing forth virgins?|Quid bonum Domini, et quid pulchrum ejus, nisi frumentum electorum, et vinum germinans virgines]]

paras.t: Relinquite infantiam, id est puerilitatis vitium et carnalitatem ; et vivite per virtutes, et ambulate per vias, id est per præcepta, prudentiæ, ut sit rationabile obsequium vestrum, et omnia ordinate agatis, atque sollicite vigiletis contra adversarios vestræ salutis : sicut in prima sua Canonica hortatur primus et summus Christi Vicarius : Estote prudentes, et vigilate in orationibus. Et denuo : Sobrii, inquit, estote, et vigilate, quia adversarius vester diabolus, tanquam leo rugiens circuit, quærens quem devoret : cui resistite, fortes in fide.
paras.en: [[9:6|Forsake childishness|Relinquite infantiam]], that is, the vice of childishness and carnality; [[9:6|and live|et vivite]] by the virtues, [[9:6|and walk by the ways|et ambulate per vias]], that is, by the precepts, [[9:6|of prudence|prudentiæ]], so that your service may be reasonable [that is, "your reasonable service", Rom 12:1], and you may do all things in order, and keep careful watch against the enemies of your salvation: as the first and highest Vicar of Christ exhorts in his first Canonical Epistle: [[1 Pet 4:7|Be prudent|Estote prudentes]], [[1 Pet 4:7|and watch in prayers|et vigilate in orationibus]]. And again: [[1 Pet 5:8|Be sober|Sobrii]], he says, [[1 Pet 5:8|and watch: because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, goeth about seeking whom he may devour|et vigilate, quia adversarius vester diabolus, tanquam leo rugiens circuit, quærens quem devoret]]: [[1 Pet 5:9|Whom resist ye, strong in faith|cui resistite, fortes in fide]].

paras.t: Qui erudit derisorem, quem scit esse talem, et in sua perversitate obduratum ac incorrigibilem, ipse sibi injuriam facit, id est, se ipsum inhonorat, imprudenter agendo atque inaniter laborando, et derisorem provocando ad injuriandum sibi. Quid ergo aget prælatus habens subditos derisores, nisi ut quos verbis nequit instruere, verberibus et per viam rigoris, quantum potest, reprimat et castiget, si forsan vexatio illis tribuat intellectum ? Sunt etenim refrenandi, ne inficiant alios.
paras.en: [[9:7|He that teacheth a scorner|Qui erudit derisorem]], whom he knows to be such, and hardened in his perversity and incorrigible, [[9:7|doth an injury to himself|ipse sibi injuriam facit]], that is, dishonours himself, by acting imprudently and labouring in vain, and by provoking the scorner to do him injury. What then shall a prelate do who has scorners among his subjects, but restrain and chastise, as far as he can, with blows and by the way of severity, those whom he cannot instruct with words, if perhaps vexation may give them understanding[[Is 28:19||]]? For they must be curbed, lest they infect others.

paras.t: Et qui arguit impium, qui, ut dictum est, incorrigibilis et induratus esse cognoscitur, sibi maculam generat, quum agat insipienter, et provocet impium ad detrahendum sibi. Talis ergo arguendus est disciplinis justitiæ, sicut jam tetigi. Noli arguere derisorem, ne oderit te, ne scilicet ad pejora incitetur, et reddat tibi malum pro bono. Hinc loquitur Dominus : Nolite sanctum dare canibus, neque mittatis margaritas vestras ante porcos, ne forte conculcent eas pedibus suis, et conversi dirumpant vos.
paras.en: [[9:7|and he that rebuketh a wicked man|Et qui arguit impium]], who, as has been said, is known to be incorrigible and hardened, [[9:7|getteth himself a blot|sibi maculam generat]], since he acts unwisely and provokes the wicked man to disparage him. Such a man, then, is to be rebuked with the chastisements of justice[[Prov 3:11||]], as I have already touched on. [[9:8|Rebuke not a scorner, lest he hate thee|Noli arguere derisorem, ne oderit te]], that is, lest he be stirred up to worse things and return thee evil for good. Hence the Lord says: [[Matt 7:6|Give not that which is holy to dogs; neither cast ye your pearls before swine, lest perhaps they trample them under their feet, and turning upon you, they tear you.|Nolite sanctum dare canibus, neque mittatis margaritas vestras ante porcos, ne forte conculcent eas pedibus suis, et conversi dirumpant vos]]

paras.t: Ideo, teste Hieronymo, perversum ac induratum ad majorem insaniam provocare, et non aliud quam odium quærere, extremæ dementiæ est. Dum ergo non est spes de alterius correctione, cessare aut differri debet correptio et exhiberi oratio. Nempe, ut Petrus Ravennensis fatetur, perversum corripere, nil aliud est quam stimulare insanum, et camino oleum adhibere, ac ventis incendia velle exstinguere. Nihilo minus, si alicujus perversitas sit nociva bono communi, non est ejus castigatio omittenda ex causa præhabita, videlicet ne odiat corrigentem, et ne ad deteriora labatur ; sed tunc per pœnas est coercendus. Et in hoc casu loquitur Origenes : Dum sacerdotes uni parent, toti Ecclesiæ moliuntur interitum. Quæ est pietas ista, uni parcere, et omnes mittere in discrimen? Polluitur enim ex uno impio populus, sicut ex una morbida ove grex inficitur universus. Et Augustinus : Molestus est, inquit, medicus furenti phrenetico, cum ligando, et pater indisciplinato filio, cum redarguendo : si autem negligant eos et perire permittant, falsa est mansuetudo hæc et crudelis. Hinc ait Bernardus : Dum increpantur vitia, et scandala inde nascuntur, ipse sibi scandali causa est, qui fecit id quod argui debuit, non ille qui arguit. Ne ergo timeas veritatem esse contra caritatem, si unius scandalum, multorum recompensaveris pace.
paras.en: Therefore, as Jerome witnesses, to provoke a perverse and hardened man to greater madness, and to seek nothing but hatred, is the height of folly. So when there is no hope of another's amendment, rebuke ought to cease or be put off, and prayer be offered instead. Indeed, as Peter of Ravenna [that is, St. Peter Chrysologus] declares, to rebuke a perverse man is nothing else than to goad a madman, to pour oil on a furnace, and to try to put out a blaze with the winds. Nevertheless, if someone's perversity is harmful to the common good, his chastisement is not to be left off for the reason given above, namely lest he hate the one correcting him and slide into worse things; but then he must be restrained by punishments. And in this case Origen says: While priests spare one man, they are working the ruin of the whole Church. What sort of mercy is this, to spare one and put all in danger? For a people is defiled by one wicked man, as a whole flock is infected by one diseased sheep. And Augustine: The physician, he says, is a trouble to the raving madman when he binds him, and the father to the undisciplined son when he rebukes him; but if they neglect them and let them perish, this gentleness is false and cruel. Hence Bernard says: When vices are rebuked and scandals arise from it, he who did what deserved rebuke is the cause of the scandal to himself, not he who rebukes. So do not fear that truth is against charity, if thou dost set the peace of many against the scandal of one.

paras.t: Argue sapientem, et diliget te : quia considerat se esse culpabilem, quum dicat apostolus Jacobus : In multis offendimus omnes. Ideo suam reprehensionem reputat medicinam, et eleemosynam spiritualem, ac beneficium esse magnum : ideo gratias agit, et diligit arguentem, quem etiam ex caritatis radice et zelo justitiæ confidit esse locutum.
paras.en: [[9:8|Rebuke a wise man, and he will love thee|Argue sapientem, et diliget te]]: because he considers that he is at fault, since the Apostle James says: [[Jas 3:2|in many things we all offend|In multis offendimus omnes]]. Therefore he reckons the reproof given him to be a medicine, a spiritual alms and a great kindness: therefore he gives thanks and loves the one who rebukes him, trusting too that he spoke from the root of charity and from zeal for justice.

paras.t: Da sapienti occasionem considerandi se ipsum atque salubria, et addetur ei sapientia : quia proficiet inde. Doce justum, et festinabit accipere salutarem doctrinam, nec erit tam improbus ut reputet se tantæ sapientiæ esse, ut eum nequeas de aliquo informare, quemadmodum Scribæ et Pharisæi, qui dixerunt cæco nato illuminato a Christo : In peccatis natus es totus, et tu doces nos ? Itaque, sicut ait Gregorius, viri vere sapientes ac timorati gratias agunt, non indignantur, eis a quibus errata sua eis panduntur, sicut præclarissimus Archiapostolus in epistola ad Galatas a Paulo notatus, in sua epistola econtrario Paulum magnifice commendavit.
paras.en: [[9:9|Give an occasion to a wise man|Da sapienti occasionem]] of considering himself and the things that make for his salvation, [[9:9|and wisdom shall be added to him|et addetur ei sapientia]]: because he will profit by it. [[9:9|Teach a just man, and he shall make haste to receive it|Doce justum, et festinabit accipere]], that is, wholesome doctrine; nor will he be so shameless as to reckon himself of such great wisdom that thou canst not inform him of anything, as did the Scribes and Pharisees, who said to the man born blind whom Christ had given sight: [[John 9:34|Thou wast wholly born in sins; and dost thou teach us?|In peccatis natus es totus, et tu doces nos?]] And so, as Gregory says, men truly wise and God-fearing give thanks to those by whom their errors are laid open to them, and are not indignant; as the most illustrious Prince of the Apostles, though reproved by Paul in the Epistle to the Galatians[[Gal 2:11||]], on the contrary commended Paul magnificently in his own epistle[[2 Pet 3:15||]][[2 Pet 3:16||]].

paras.t: Principium sapientiæ, timor Domini. Hoc jam supra expositum est. Et scientia sanctorum, prudentia. Vera namque prudentia, non nisi in virtuosis habetur hominibus, ut probat Philosophus. In malis autem et passionatis hominibus, non est vera prudentia, sed calliditas quædam vulpina et humana versutia. Passiones quippe et vitia corrumpunt in eis rectum rationis judicium, magisque propria commoda quærunt, quam bonum commune. Verumtamen scientia capitur hic extense pro practica notitia, boni efficaciter approbativa : sicque prudentiam comprehendit, quamvis proprie loquendo ab invicem distinguantur. De hac scientia salubri Dominus per Isaiam testatur : Captivus ductus est populus meus, eo quod non habuit scientiam.
paras.en: [[9:10|The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom|Principium sapientiæ, timor Domini]]. This has already been explained above[[Prov 1:7||]]. [[9:10|and the knowledge of the holy is prudence|Et scientia sanctorum, prudentia]]. For true prudence is found only in virtuous men, as the Philosopher [that is, Aristotle] proves. In wicked men and men ruled by their passions there is no true prudence, but a kind of foxlike cunning and human craftiness. For passions and vices corrupt in them the right judgment of reason, and they seek their own advantage more than the common good. Here, however, *knowledge* is taken broadly for practical knowledge that effectively approves the good: and so it includes prudence, though, properly speaking, the two are distinguished from one another. Of this wholesome knowledge the Lord testifies through Isaias: [[Is 5:13|is my people led away captive|Captivus ductus est populus meus]], [[Is 5:13|because they had not knowledge|eo quod non habuit scientiam]].

paras.t: Per me enim multiplicabuntur dies tui : id est, mihi Sapientiæ obtemperando, obtinebis vitam diuturniorem ac meliorem, moderate et sobrie te habendo, ac diversa vitando pericula. Possunt quoque per dies intelligi ipsæ virtutes, atque internæ illuminationes, quibus anima intus clarescit : quæ crescunt et perficiuntur in homine sapientiam amplectente. Et addentur tibi anni vitæ, id est dies æternitatis in gloria, juxta illud : Longitudine dierum adimplebo eum, et ostendam illi salutare meum.
paras.en: [[9:11|For by me shall thy days be multiplied|Per me enim multiplicabuntur dies tui]]: that is, by obeying me, Wisdom, thou shalt obtain a longer and better life, by conducting thyself with moderation and sobriety and avoiding various dangers. By *days* can also be understood the virtues themselves, and the inward illuminations by which the soul grows bright within: these increase and are perfected in the man who embraces wisdom. [[9:11|and years of life shall be added to thee|Et addentur tibi anni vitæ]], that is, the days of eternity in glory, according to that: [[Ps 90:16|I will fill him with length of days; and I will shew him my salvation.|Longitudine dierum adimplebo eum, et ostendam illi salutare meum]]

paras.t: Si sapiens fueris, tibimetipsi eris, id est, in propriam mercedem et gloriam tibi proficiet ac redundabit. Ex consequenti vero, sapientia alicujus est proximis suis proficua : quibus succurrit docendo, corripiendo, hortando, orando, exemplariter conversando, aut simili modo. Unde in aliquibus libris subjungitur, Et proximis tuis. Et ita allegat in suis Homiliis Eusebius, dicens : Nullius sapientis sapientia sibi soli amica est. Hoc tamen non est de textu, sed ab aliquo expositore annexum. Si autem illusor sis, solus portabis malum, id est culpam et debitam pœnam pro ea, sicut ait Apostolus : Unusquisque proprium onus portabit. Interdum tamen illusor scandalizat, perturbat ac decipit alios, sicque sua perversitas est aliis occasio culpæ et pœnæ : qui nisi libere consentirent in culpam, non eis noceret alterius pravitas, sed esset eis exercitatio ad profectum.
paras.en: [[9:12|If thou be wise, thou shalt be so to thyself|Si sapiens fueris, tibimetipsi eris]], that is, it will profit thee and redound to thine own reward and glory. Consequently, however, a man's wisdom is profitable to his neighbours, whom he helps by teaching, rebuking, exhorting, praying, living as an example, or in some like way. Hence in some books there is added: *And to thy neighbours*. And so Eusebius cites it in his Homilies, saying: No wise man's wisdom is a friend to himself alone. This, however, is not of the text, but was added by some commentator. [[9:12|and if a scorner, thou alone shalt bear the evil|Si autem illusor sis, solus portabis malum]], that is, the fault and the punishment due for it, as the Apostle says: [[Gal 6:5|every one shall bear his own burden|Unusquisque proprium onus portabit]]. Sometimes, however, the scorner scandalizes, troubles and deceives others, and so his perversity is an occasion of fault and punishment to others: yet unless they freely consented to the fault, the other's wickedness would not harm them, but would be to them an exercise for their progress.

paras.t: Porro, quod subditur, Mulier stulta et clamosa, plenaque illecebris, et nihil omnino sciens, quamvis ad litteram possit exponi de muliere adultera, libidinosa, seu fornicatrice, communiter tamen exponitur de insipientia seu falsa doctrina, et peste hæretica, quæ mentem ad spirituale adulterium, hoc est ad recedendum a Deo, a fidei veritate, a tenore justitiæ, trahit : quæ et clamorosa est et inverecunda, sicut asserit Augustinus : Sileat hæreticorum loquacitas, nullam habens verecundiam, et plena illecebris, quoniam turpiter delectatur, et ad fœda corporis delectamenta inducit.
paras.en: Further, what follows, [[9:13|A foolish woman and clamorous, and full of allurements, and knowing nothing at all|Mulier stulta et clamosa, plenaque illecebris, et nihil omnino sciens]], though in the letter it can be explained of an adulterous woman, a lustful woman or a harlot, is commonly explained of folly or false doctrine, and the plague of heresy, which draws the mind to spiritual adultery, that is, to departing from God, from the truth of the faith, from the course of justice: which is both clamorous and shameless, as Augustine asserts: Let the loquacity of heretics be silent, which has no shame; and [[9:13|full of allurements|plena illecebris]], since it takes a shameful delight, and leads men on to the foul delights of the body.

paras.t: Sedet in foribus domus suæ, id est in locis patentibus congregationis hæreticæ, seu insanæ ac fatuæ, super sellam, id est sedem, in excelso urbis loco, id est in principibus et prælatis suæ societatis atque communitatis, quia per illos allicit alios ; ut vocaret transeuntes per viam, et pergentes in itinere suo, id est, fideles, per viam salutis ac fidei catholicæ tendentes ad patriam, incorporaret suæ congregationi iniquæ, involvendo ipsos suis erroribus ; dicens : Quis est parvulus? Declinet ad me. Simili modo Sapientia increata, sicut jam patuit, ad se vocat et exhortatur. Sicque insipientia et pravitas hæretica conformant se partim in verbis, veræ fidei ac Sapientiæ sanctæ, quatenus sub specie boni magis decipiant. Ait itaque, Si quis est parvulus : quasi dicat, Ego quoque humiles quæro et approbo.
paras.en: [[9:14|Sat at the door of her house|Sedet in foribus domus suæ]], that is, in the open places of the heretical, or mad and foolish, congregation, [[9:14|upon a seat|super sellam]], that is, a chair, [[9:14|in a high place of the city|in excelso urbis loco]], that is, in the princes and prelates of her society and community, because through them she entices others; [[9:15|To call them that pass by the way, and go on their journey|ut vocaret transeuntes per viam, et pergentes in itinere suo]], that is, to incorporate into her wicked congregation the faithful who are making their way to the fatherland by the way of salvation and of the Catholic faith, entangling them in her errors; saying: [[9:16|He that is a little one, let him turn to me|Quis est parvulus? Declinet ad me]] [Denis reads "Who is a little one?"]. In like manner uncreated Wisdom, as has already appeared, calls and exhorts to herself[[9:4||]]. And so folly and heretical wickedness conform themselves in part, in their words, to the true faith and to holy Wisdom, so as to deceive the more under the appearance of good. She says, then, *Whosoever is a little one*: as if to say, I too seek out and approve the humble.

paras.t: Et vecordi, id est stulto, locuta est : Aquæ furtivæ dulciores sunt, et panis absconditus suavior. Per aquas furtivas, intelliguntur doctrinæ hæreticæ et perversæ, quæ primo in secreto docentur quousque prævaleant. Hæ autem doctrinæ sunt multis tanto delectabiliores, quanto minus transcendunt capacitatem et ratiocinationem intellectus humani, quem difficile est in captivitatem redigere ad credendum ea quæ omnem rationem, experientiam et sensum excedunt : sicut quod Arius docuit, Deum non esse trinum in Personis : et Photinus, quod Christus sit purus homo ; et alii quidam, quod in Sacramento non sit Christus, nisi ut in signo. Tales quoque doctrinæ recedunt ab arcta via salutis, et delectabilia multa licentiant, a quibus sapientia vera refrenat : ideo dulciores videntur. Panis autem absconditus, est sacrificium superstitiosum talium perversorum, vel in se, vel quantum ad modum sacrilegum, quo illud sacrificant et frequentant. Vel, Panis absconditus, est error occultus, latens perfidia, lex iniqua : quibus reficitur homo vecors ac perfidus. Denique, ad litteram, multis dulcius sapiunt cibus et potus, quem occulte et furtive accipiunt, in quantum in tali refectione propria libertas plus aliquid habet, vel proprium separatumque commodum magis sentitur, vel diabolus magis instigat, prout in libro Confessionum in simili tangit Augustinus, et in Collationibus Patrum abbas Serapion sibi in sua juventute contigisse fatetur de paxemade, quam comedit quotidie in secreto. Sed istud in virtuosis locum non habet. Conformiter de spiritualibus aquis furtivis ac pane abscondito, in perversis perfidisque hominibus accidit.
paras.en: [[9:16|And to the fool|Et vecordi]], that is, to the foolish man, [[9:16|she said|locuta est]]: [[9:17|Stolen waters are sweeter, and hidden bread is more pleasant.|Aquæ furtivæ dulciores sunt, et panis absconditus suavior.]] By *stolen waters* are understood heretical and perverse doctrines, which are at first taught in secret until they prevail. These doctrines are the more delightful to many the less they go beyond the capacity and reasoning of the human understanding, which it is hard to bring into captivity so as to believe things that exceed all reason, experience and sense: as Arius taught that God is not three in Persons, and Photinus that Christ is a mere man, and certain others that Christ is not in the Sacrament except as in a sign. Such doctrines also depart from the narrow way of salvation, and permit many pleasures from which true wisdom holds men back: therefore they seem sweeter. And the *hidden bread* is the superstitious sacrifice of such perverse men, either in itself or as to the sacrilegious manner in which they offer it and frequent it. Or, *hidden bread* is hidden error, lurking faithlessness, a wicked law: with which the foolish and faithless man is fed. Lastly, in the letter, food and drink taken secretly and by stealth taste sweeter to many, inasmuch as in such a meal one's own freedom has something more, or one's own separate advantage is more felt, or the devil urges more strongly: as Augustine touches on in a like matter in the book of the Confessions, and as in the Conferences of the Fathers the abbot Serapion confesses happened to him in his youth with the *paxamas* [a small hard-baked biscuit or rusk, the monks' bread] which he ate every day in secret. But this has no place in the virtuous. In like manner it happens with the spiritual stolen waters and hidden bread in perverse and faithless men.

paras.t: Et ignoravit insipientia seu hæresis detestanda, quod gigantes ibi sint, id est, spiritus maligni et superbissimi hæresiarchæ, in suis doctrinis dominentur ac regnent, non Deus nec sapientia salutaris. Istud enim despicit credere, et putat pertinaci animo se bene sentire : imo incorrigibiliter suis adhæret erroribus usque ad ignem. Et in profundis inferni convivæ ejus, id est, quod hi qui participant, et adhærent suis doctrinis, in profundo inferni demergantur, sicut scriptum est : Qui non credit, jam judicatus est, quia non credit in nomine unigeniti Filii Dei. Unde rursus in prima sua epistola ait idem Evangelista : Qui non credit in Filium, mendacem facit Patrem, quia non credit in testimonium quo testificatus est Pater de Filio suo.
paras.en: [[9:18|And he did not know|Et ignoravit]], that is, folly or detestable heresy, [[9:18|that giants are there|quod gigantes ibi sint]], that is, that evil spirits and most proud heresiarchs rule and reign in her doctrines, not God nor saving wisdom. For she disdains to believe this, and thinks with a stubborn mind that she judges rightly: nay, she clings incorrigibly to her errors even unto the fire. [[9:18|and that her guests are in the depths of hell|Et in profundis inferni convivæ ejus]], that is, that those who share in and cling to her doctrines are plunged into the depth of hell, as it is written: [[John 3:18|he that doth not believe is already judged: because he believeth not in the name of the only begotten Son of God|Qui non credit, jam judicatus est, quia non credit in nomine unigeniti Filii Dei]]. Hence again the same Evangelist says in his first epistle: [[1 John 5:10|He that believeth not the Son maketh him a liar: because he believeth not in the testimony which God hath testified of his Son|Qui non credit in Filium, mendacem facit Patrem, quia non credit in testimonium quo testificatus est Pater de Filio suo]] [Denis reads "maketh the Father a liar" and "which the Father hath testified"].

paras.t: Ideo subditur : qui enim applicabitur illi, id est, insipientiæ aut hæreticæ pravitati consentit, descendet ad inferos : nam qui abscesserit ab ea, salvabitur, nisi aliunde sit reus. Verumtamen versus iste non est de textu.
paras.en: Therefore it is added: *For he that shall be joined to her*, that is, who consents to folly or to heretical wickedness, *shall go down to hell; but he that departeth from her, shall be saved* [this addition, found after v. 18 in the Clementine Vulgate, is not in the Douay-Rheims text of this app], unless he be guilty on some other count. However, this verse is not of the text.
